summary: performance lens over ASKFLOOR-1-T6 (13 product path(s), 401a889..d681c84, Codex via the autoreview skill at --max-priority P2): 1 blocking, 3 non-blocking. The inline implementation fails to reset the process-wide outage latch after a successful automatic allow, so later outages in that conversation may not notify. The change also introduces a prohibited dead duplicate sender API, and the new invariance and aggregation tests do not exercise or observe several explicitly required performance and outage behaviors.

blocking_findings.summary: [P1] Remove the unused duplicate outage-notice entry point (apps/core/src/runtime/permission-judge-outage.ts:133): `sendJudgeOfflineNotice` is a newly exported second implementation of the notice sender, but both production call sites in this change use `sendJudgeOfflineNoticeForRequest`; its only caller in the bundle is the new glue test.

non_blocking_findings.summary: [P2] Clear the inline outage latch before returning an answered allow (apps/core/src/app/bootstrap/inline-agent-loop-tools.ts:422): The inline path returns immediately for an automatic classifier allow before reaching `observeJudgeAvailabilityForRequest`.

[P2] Make the invariance test observe the required offline behavior (apps/core/test/unit/runtime/askfloor-invariance.test.ts:30): This test uses only the IPC replay result (`taps`, decider, source, and rail provenance) and compares unavailable runs directly with answered runs.

[P2] Include all required scenarios in the aggregation run (apps/core/test/unit/runtime/askfloor-tap-budget.test.ts:351): Despite its title, this aggregation samples a few scenarios and does not execute TB1–TB4 plus their mirror fixtures in every required lane; for example there is no native `FileWrite` TB4 replay and none of the protected-write, outside-workspace, scheduler-delete, or raw-path-attach mirrors are aggregated.
